newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee weakened against the dollar and pound on Friday in line with international trends, commercial bank forex dealers said.
The rupee was posted at a mean commercial rate of 20.3360 against the dollar from 20.2965 on Thursday. The rupee weakened to a mean of 31.8715 for one pound from 31.8115 on Thursday.
"We fixed the rupee lower today (Friday) since the dollar went up in overnight markets," one money dealer said.

The dealer said the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate put pounds on tender to banks on Friday morning. From the 1996 harvest season, the Syndicate can sell 25 percent of the island's sugar export proceeds directly to banks.
Previously, all sugar proceeds were kept by the central bank, which then sold them to commercial banks through interventions.
The money dealer said a couple of commercial banks were still short hard currency despite central bank intervention on Thursday mid-afternoon.
He added the central bank sold dollars in a Thursday intervention, but commercial banks did not get the entire amount they asked for.
"Such drip feeding during the intervention did not completely relieve the shortage situation in those banks' reserves," the dealer said.
